answer: Forced-Divergence Challenge Ledger. Each identity must answer a fresh, context-specific challenge whose correct response depends on its private history; a clone can only copy its twin. Answers are recorded as signed steps on a shared ledger, and any two identities answering identically within a window are flagged. The attacker must either pay humans to maintain genuinely divergent records along a costly canyon of forks, or lose the clone. Honest identities face no penalty; clones pay a per-identity terrace of irreducible divergence work. Over time this builds an opal of verifiable uniqueness,
